transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, what brought me in is... I keep forgetting things at work. Like scheduled callbacks, work orders, that kind of thing. Which is really frustrating because we just switched to this new digital tablet system for our tickets, and I swear, the glare on those screens when you're up on a roof fixing an AC compressor is just terrible. I don't know whose bright idea it was to give maintenance crews glass screens, honestly. 

But yeah, I'm forgetting even basic follow-ups I promised people, and it’s piled up so much lately that my work actually sent me here. They told me I need to get it sorted out before I lose my shot at moving up to a senior spot. Which would really be a shame, because my buddy Mike just got promoted to senior crew last month and he says the new dispatch trucks they give you have heated seats, and with my lower back acting up in the winters lately, that would be a lifesaver... but anyway, yeah, that's why I'm here.
Have you always had trouble remembering things or is this a relatively new problem for you?

Oh, no, it's not new at all. I remember being exactly like this way back in grade school, long before I had any of this pressure from work. My teachers always told my parents I was a bright kid, but I was just constantly misplacing my papers. I'd always miss parts of the directions they gave us, or I'd need someone to come over and remind me to actually finish my classwork. 

Which is funny to think about, because back then we used those really rough-feeling paper tablets—I think they were called Big Chief or something?—and they had those giant wide lines. I always loved the smell of that paper. Actually, thinking about my old elementary school, I always remember how those giant cast-iron radiators would just clank and bang all winter long. Now that I do maintenance for a living, whenever I hear a radiator making that noise, it drives me absolutely crazy because I know it just needs the valve bled. It's almost always just trapped air in the pipes, and it takes two seconds with a radiator key to fix it. But the janitor never did. So we just sat there listening to it bang all day while I stared at the wall forgetting to finish my spelling sheet. But anyway, yeah, it's definitely been a lifelong thing for me.
Do you often find yourself having trouble paying attention or staying focused on tasks?

Yeah, all the time. It's like... okay, so I'll pull up one of those digital work orders on the tablet, right? And I start reading the notes the dispatcher put in, thinking, okay, I've got this. But then halfway through the paragraph, my mind just completely slips off. Maybe I hear a compressor kick on somewhere, or I start thinking about the next job on my list, and suddenly I realize I'm staring at the screen and I have absolutely no idea what I just looked at. 

It's actually a lot like when you're trying to trace a wire through a drop ceiling. You start at the junction box, and you're following the red wire, but then you see this whole rat's nest of old CAT5 cables from like, 1998, just abandoned up there. I hate when people do that, just leave dead cable instead of pulling it out. It's a fire hazard, honestly, plus it just looks sloppy. My first boss, old man Henderson, he used to make us pull every single inch of dead wire before we could run anything new. He was a real stickler. But anyway, yeah, tracing the wire—you get distracted by the mess, and suddenly you've lost the red wire you were supposed to be following. That's what reading those work orders feels like. I just lose the thread completely.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're supposed to be sitting still?

No, I don't really think so. I can sit still just fine. Like, when I'm in the dispatch van waiting on a call, I just sit there without any problem. Though, honestly, sitting in those vans is a literal pain anyway because the seats are completely shot. The springs on the driver's side of my van are just gone. 

I told the fleet manager about it—his name's Gary, nice guy, but he's always trying to cut corners on the budget. Like, he keeps buying these generic windshield wipers for the fleet that streak the second it even drizzles. We had this huge storm last Tuesday, just absolute buckets of rain, and I'm trying to merge onto the interstate and I can't see a thing because Gary's cheap wipers are just smearing road grime all over the glass. It's incredibly dangerous, especially with the way people drive around here. I actually had to pull over under an overpass just to wait it out, and I ended up watching this guy try to change a tire in the mud. He had the jack placed completely wrong, totally missing the pinch weld, and I almost got out in the pouring rain to help him before he crushed his rocker panel, but... 

Wait, what were you asking me? Oh, right, fidgeting. No, I don't really get restless or anything like that.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Not really. I mean, I don't think I do things without thinking. I'm actually pretty careful, especially with my tools. You have to be, you know? Like, my multimeter—it's a Fluke, one of the really good ones. I saved up for it because the company-issued ones are basically useless if you're trying to get a precise reading on a low-voltage system. 

Speaking of low voltage, I got called out to this fancy new apartment complex last week because their intercom system was down. The whole building is supposed to be "smart," but it's really just a nightmare of cheap sensors. Anyway, I get to the main panel, and whoever wired it didn't label a single thing. Not one piece of tape, not a sharpie mark, nothing. Just a giant spaghetti bowl of wires. It drives me insane when contractors do that. They just want to get in, get paid, and get out, and they leave the mess for the maintenance crew to figure out years later. I spent three hours just toning out lines to figure out which one went to the front door relay. And the property manager kept hovering over me, asking when it would be fixed. Like, lady, I don't have x-ray vision, I can't just magically know where these wires go. 

But yeah, I don't really do things on impulse. I'm pretty methodical about stuff.
Have you been feeling overwhelmed or stressed about your work situation or anything else lately?

Yeah, I guess I am. It's... it's gotten pretty bad, actually. The whole thing has turned into a really serious work issue. I've got this massive backlog of work orders just piling up, and now there are tenant complaints because I'm taking too long to get to things. They even put a safety review on my record, which is just... I mean, I've been working so hard toward this promotion to lead technician, and I'm terrified this is going to cost me the whole path. 

It's just so frustrating because I know how to do the work. Like, the safety review? That was over a lockout/tagout procedure on a boiler unit. I know the procedure backward and forward. The tags we use are these heavy-duty plastic ones, the red ones with the white lettering, you know? They're supposed to be indestructible, but the zip ties they give us to attach them are so cheap. They snap if it's too cold out. I keep telling Gary—remember Gary from fleet? He orders the safety supplies too—I keep telling him we need the industrial nylon ties, not the cheap plastic ones from the dollar bin. I actually brought my own zip ties from home for a while, the black UV-resistant ones. My husband bought a huge bucket of them at a hardware store liquidation sale a couple years ago. The hardware store was run by this family, the Millers, for like forty years, and then one of those big box stores moved in across the highway and just completely ran them out of business in less than a year. It's really sad, honestly. They had the best fastener aisle in town, you could buy individual screws instead of having to buy a box of a hundred when you only need three... 

But anyway, the safety review. It's on my record now, along with the complaints and the backlog, and I just... I feel like I'm drowning, and I'm so scared I'm going to lose my shot at that promotion.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

No, not really sad. I mean, I get frustrated with everything going on at work, obviously, but I wouldn't say I'm walking around depressed or crying or anything. I mostly just want to come home and relax at the end of the day, you know? Just sit on the couch and zone out. 

Though honestly, my couch is getting so uncomfortable lately. We bought it at this discount furniture warehouse out on Route 9 a few years ago. Huge place, they used to have one of those giant inflatable gorillas on the roof. I don't know why furniture places always use the gorilla. Car dealerships do it too. There's a used car lot right down the street from my dispatch center that has one, but the blower motor on it is clearly dying, so the gorilla just sort of slumps over the cars like it's exhausted. I actually told the owner—because I was out there fixing their exterior security lighting—I said, 'Buddy, you need a new centrifugal fan for that thing before the motor burns out completely.' But he didn't want to hear it. People never want to spend money on preventative maintenance. They just wait until the thing completely breaks and then it's suddenly a massive emergency and they want you there in five minutes. Like the HVAC system at the... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Was it about being depressed? Yeah, no, I don't think I'm sad. Just... stressed out, mostly.
Do you have intense emotional reactions to things that happen to you?

No, I wouldn't say intense. I mean, I don't fly off the handle or anything. I get annoyed, sure, like when I'm trying to finish a job and my radio keeps squawking with people asking for updates. Our two-way radios are absolute garbage, by the way. The batteries won't hold a charge for more than four hours, so you're constantly swapping them out. I keep a spare on the charger in the van, but the charger itself has this loose contact on the third pin, so you have to wiggle it just right until the little red light comes on. I actually tried to resolder it last week, but the casing is sealed with these proprietary security screws—the ones with the little pin in the middle of the star? I have a whole set of security bits I got from a catalog, but of course, I lost the exact size I needed for this one. I probably dropped it in an elevator shaft or something. You drop a tool down an elevator shaft, and it's just gone forever. Into the void. I once lost a really nice pair of wire strippers down one at the old mercantile building downtown. That building has these gorgeous original brass elevator doors from the 1920s, but the tracks are always getting jammed because people drop trash in the grooves. I spend half my time just digging out pennies and gum wrappers with a flathead screwdriver... 

But no, I don't have intense emotional reactions. I'm pretty level-headed, I think. Just easily annoyed by the radios and stuff.
Do you have trouble organizing your time or tasks?

No, I don't think I have trouble organizing things. I mean, I'm pretty good about keeping track of what I need to do. I use this heavy-duty aluminum clipboard for all my work orders. It's one of those contractor ones that opens up on a hinge so you can store extra paperwork and pens inside. I actually got it from a delivery driver who used to drop off plumbing fixtures at my old job. Frank, I think his name was. Or maybe Fred? No, Frank. 

He drove this massive, ancient diesel box truck that smelled just awful, like burnt oil and French fries. He said he ran it on biodiesel he made himself in his garage. People do that, you know? They go to restaurants and ask for their used fryer oil. There's this diner near my house, Mama's Kitchen, they make the best curly fries, but their grease trap is an absolute nightmare to clean out. I had to snake their main drain once, and the amount of congealed grease was just... it was like concrete. You really need a high-pressure water jetter for that kind of blockage, but my boss at the time wouldn't authorize the rental fee for the equipment, so I was stuck out in the alley for six hours with just a manual auger. My arms were sore for a week after that. You really don't realize how much upper body strength you need for plumbing until you're fighting fifty feet of steel cable in the freezing rain... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about my schedule or something? But yeah, no, I keep everything organized on my clipboard just fine.
Do you find it hard to calm down after something upsetting happens?

No, not really. I mean, if something really bad happens, sure, it takes a minute, but I don't stay worked up forever. Like, I can usually just let it go and move on to the next thing. 

I try to just keep moving, you know? Like when I'm at the hardware store. I spend so much time at the hardware store, I swear I should just get a cot and sleep in aisle four. Aisle four is where they keep all the fasteners—screws, bolts, washers, all of it. But the way they organize it makes absolutely no sense. They have the metric bolts mixed in right next to the standard ones, and the little plastic baggies are always ripped open because people try to test-fit them and then just shove them back in the wrong bin. It drives me crazy. I was looking for a specific size toggle bolt last Tuesday for this drywall repair I was doing at a dental office. Dentists always have the weirdest lighting fixtures. They're these heavy, articulating arms that pull down over the chair, and if they aren't anchored straight into the stud, they just rip right out of the wall. Anyway, the dentist there, Dr. Evans, he has this massive saltwater fish tank in the waiting room. It's beautiful, really, with these bright blue tangs and clownfish. But saltwater tanks are a nightmare to maintain. The salt creep gets everywhere, it corrodes all the metal fittings, and the filtration systems are so loud if you don't pad the pumps right. I used to have a freshwater tank when I was a kid, just goldfish, mostly. They get huge if you put them in a big enough tank, though most people just keep them in those tiny little bowls where they can't even turn around...

I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought. What was the question again? Something about being upset? But yeah, no, I calm down pretty quick. I don't hold onto things.
Do you find yourself getting easily irritated by small things that wouldn't normally bother you?

No, I don't think so. Small things don't really get to me. Well, except maybe when painters just spray right over door hinges and strike plates instead of taping them off. That's just lazy, you know? 

I spent three hours on Tuesday trying to scrape layers of cheap gloss enamel off a strike plate in unit 4B. The tenant there, Mrs. Higgins, she's a sweetheart, though. She always bakes these little lemon bars whenever I come over to fix things. Lemon is actually my absolute favorite flavor for desserts. My grandmother used to have this huge Meyer lemon tree in her backyard down in Florida. The citrus bugs got to it eventually, though. Those little aphids just destroy everything if you don't spray neem oil on the leaves early enough in the season. 

Neem oil smells absolutely terrible, by the way. It's kind of like garlic and sulfur mixed together. I actually spilled a bottle of it in the trunk of my Chevy Nova back in '98, and I swear, no matter how much baking soda I dumped on the carpet, that car smelled like a rotten salad dressing factory until the day the transmission finally blew on the interstate. Getting towed off the highway is terrifying, the way the semis just blow right past you so fast the whole car shakes... 

Wait, I'm sorry. Did you ask if I get irritated? No, I'm pretty easygoing, honestly. Small stuff is just small stuff.
Do you have mood swings?

No, I don't really have mood swings. I mean, my mood is pretty steady most days. I just wake up, get my coffee, and go to work. 

I have to have my coffee first thing, though. I use this old French press I found at a flea market years ago. It's got this beautiful copper housing around the glass, but the plunger is a little bent, so if you don't push it down perfectly straight, the grounds shoot up the side and you end up drinking gritty coffee. There's nothing worse than getting a mouthful of coffee grounds when you're just trying to wake up. It reminds me of this time I had to fix a garbage disposal at this apartment complex over on 5th Street. The tenant had shoved, I kid you not, an entire bag of potting soil down the sink because they thought the disposal would just "grind it up and wash it away." The whole P-trap was packed solid with dirt and perlite. Perlite is that little white stuff they put in potting soil to help with drainage, you know? It's actually a type of volcanic glass that expands when you heat it up, kind of like popcorn. I read about it once in this gardening magazine I found in a waiting room. I always try to read the magazines in waiting rooms, but they're always like three years out of date. Like, why am I reading about the 2019 summer Olympics in 2022? It just doesn't make sense to keep them around that long...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Mood swings? Yeah, no, I don't really have those. I'm pretty even-keeled.
Do you have trouble controlling your emotions when something unexpected happens?

No, I don't think so. I'm pretty good at rolling with the punches. In my line of work, you kind of have to be, because nothing ever goes the way you expect it to. 

Like yesterday, I was supposed to just swap out a leaky faucet in this older house, built in maybe the 1950s. Simple job, right? Take off the old one, put on the new one. But when I went to shut off the water under the sink, the shut-off valve—the original one from when the house was built—just crumbled in my hand. It was completely corroded. So suddenly, I've got water spraying everywhere, and I have to run out to the street to shut off the main water line. The water meter cover was stuck, of course, and I had to pry it up with a crowbar. I keep a really nice titanium crowbar in my truck for things like that. Titanium is great because it's so much lighter than steel, but it doesn't rust. I actually got it on sale at this little hardware store that was going out of business. It's so sad when those independent places close down. They always have the best stuff, and the people who work there actually know what they're talking about, unlike the big box stores where you ask a teenager where the PVC primer is and they look at you like you're speaking Greek. My grandfather used to run a hardware store in Ohio. He had these old wooden floors that would creak every time you walked down the aisles, and he smelled like sawdust and pipe tobacco. Nobody really smokes pipe tobacco anymore, do they? It's all just those little electronic things that smell like cotton candy...

Wait, I'm sorry. Did you ask about my emotions? No, I don't lose control or anything. I just deal with it. You have to, you know?
Do you find that your emotions often shift rapidly without an obvious reason?

No, not really. My emotions don't just bounce around for no reason. I feel like there's always a cause, you know? Even if it's just being tired or hungry. 

Speaking of being hungry, I've been trying to eat more protein lately. I read somewhere that it helps keep your energy levels stable throughout the day. I started buying these little packets of tuna, the ones that come in different flavors? The lemon pepper one is pretty good, but the jalapeño one is way too spicy for me. I don't know how people eat super spicy food. I had a roommate in my twenties who would put hot sauce on literally everything—eggs, pizza, even macaroni and cheese. She had this whole collection of hot sauces lined up on the kitchen counter. Some of the labels were hilarious, like "Devil's Breath" and stuff like that. She actually ended up moving to New Mexico, which makes sense because they put green chiles on everything out there. I visited her once, and the sky out there is just... it's so big and blue. It doesn't look real. We went to this alien museum in Roswell, which was kind of cheesy but fun. They had all these little green men statues everywhere. It's funny how we always picture aliens as little green men with big eyes. Why not purple or orange? I guess green just stuck in pop culture. 

Wait, what was the question? Rapid shifts? Oh, no. I'm pretty steady. No sudden shifts out of nowhere.
Do you think your difficulties with paying attention and remembering things are affecting your relationships with friends and family?

Well, with friends and family... I mean, they get frustrated with me sometimes when I forget to call back or zone out when they're talking. But honestly, the real problem is at work. It's turned into a serious issue lately. I've got this massive backlog of work orders I just can't seem to get through, and the tenants are starting to complain. 

The property manager even had to put a safety review on my record because I left a ladder and some tools out in a hallway overnight. I just completely forgot they were there because I went to grab a specific drill bit from my truck and got sidetracked fixing the latch on the truck cap. Those caps are so finicky, especially the fiberglass ones. If the struts go bad, you're basically lifting a dead weight every time you open it. I replaced the struts on mine last winter. I ordered them online from this auto parts place that ships out of Michigan. My cousin lives in Michigan, up in the Upper Peninsula. Have you ever been up there? It's gorgeous, but the winters are absolutely brutal. They get "lake effect" snow, which means the cold air picks up moisture from the Great Lakes and just dumps feet of snow all at once. My cousin sent me a picture once where the snow was literally up to the roof of his garage. He has to use a roof rake to pull the snow off so the roof doesn't cave in. I can't even imagine having to do that. I hate being cold. That's why I always wear these insulated Carhartt overalls when I have to work outside in the winter. They're so stiff when you first buy them, you practically have to wash them ten times before you can bend your knees...

Oh, shoot, sorry. I'm doing it again. What was I saying? Right, work. Yeah, I'm really scared because I've been working toward this promotion to lead maintenance supervisor, and with the backlog and the safety review... I'm terrified this is going to cost me the promotion.
Do you think your difficulties with paying attention and remembering things are affecting your personal relationships outside of work?

I mean, not really? Like I said, they get annoyed sometimes, but it's not like it's ruining my marriage or anything. My husband knows how I am. He just kind of sighs and repeats himself. We've been married for almost twenty years, so he's used to it. 

We actually had our anniversary last month. We went to this Italian place downtown that we've been wanting to try forever. It's one of those places where they make the pasta fresh right in front of you. You can see them kneading the dough through this big glass window. It takes a lot of arm strength to knead dough like that for hours. I tried making homemade bread once during the pandemic, like everybody else did, right? The sourdough starter thing. I named mine "Doughlene" like the Dolly Parton song. But I kept forgetting to feed it, and it just turned gray and smelled like old beer, so I had to throw it out. It's a shame because I love fresh sourdough. Especially toasted with a lot of butter. Real butter, not the margarine stuff. My mom used to buy margarine in these big plastic tubs, and she'd save the tubs to put leftovers in. So you'd open the fridge thinking you were getting butter, and it would be like, leftover spaghetti. It's funny how moms from that generation all did the same things. Like keeping the good guest towels in the bathroom that nobody was allowed to use. What's the point of a towel you can't dry your hands on? They just sit there collecting dust. 

Anyway... no, my personal relationships are mostly fine. It's just the work stuff that's really got me stressed out right now.
Have you ever been diagnosed with or treated for ADHD?

No, never. I don't really go to the doctor much anyway unless I have to. The last time I went was for a physical when I got hired at the property management company. They make you do this whole screening to make sure you can lift fifty pounds and all that. The clinic they sent me to had the most uncomfortable chairs in the waiting room. They were those hard plastic ones, like they have in schools? I don't know why places don't invest in better seating. 

And the magazines were all from like three years ago. I was flipping through this old issue of some home and garden magazine, and there was this article about landscaping with native plants. Which makes a lot of sense, because if you plant stuff that's naturally from your area, you don't have to water it as much. We have these hydrangea bushes at one of the properties I work at, and they are such water hogs. If it doesn't rain for two days, they just wilt and look completely pathetic. The tenants are always calling saying the bushes are dying, but they just need a good soak. I ended up setting up a drip irrigation line for them so I wouldn't have to keep dragging a hose out there. Hoses are such a pain to coil back up, especially when it's chilly out and the rubber gets all stiff... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, being diagnosed. No, nobody's ever told me I had anything like that or treated me for it.
Do you think your difficulties with paying attention and remembering things are more related to your work environment or an inherent part of how your mind works?

I think it's just... how my brain is wired. Because I remember being exactly this way back in grade school, way, way before I ever had any of this job pressure. My teachers always told my parents I was a bright kid, but I was constantly misplacing my papers. 

My mom actually bought me one of those Trapper Keepers to try and help me stay organized. Do you remember those? They had that big Velcro flap that made that loud ripping sound every time you opened it in the middle of quiet reading time. I had one with a neon pink grid and a dolphin on it. I think it was Lisa Frank? Her stuff was everywhere back then. Everybody had the folders and the pencils. Pencils used to be so much better, honestly. The wood actually sharpened evenly. Now when you buy pencils, the lead is always broken all the way down the middle, so you sharpen it and the tip just falls right out. It drives me crazy at work when I'm trying to mark a measurement on a piece of drywall and my pencil tip just snaps off. And then you have to fish your utility knife out of your pocket to whittle it down because the sharpener is all the way out in the truck. Drywall dust gets absolutely everywhere, too, it just coats your boots and dries out your hands...

Oh, geez, sorry. I lost my train of thought again. Um, but yeah, back in school... my teachers said I'd just miss parts of the directions all the time, and they constantly had to come over and remind me to actually finish my classwork. So it's definitely not just the work environment. It's just always been me.
Have you ever had a comprehensive evaluation for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder?

I mean, I don't think so? Like I said, I haven't really been to the doctor much. What does a comprehensive evaluation even look like? Is it like a bunch of tests or something? I've always hated tests. In high school, I used to freeze up whenever they handed out those Scantron sheets. The ones where you had to bubble in the answers with a number two pencil. If you didn't erase completely, the machine would mark it wrong. I always worried I wasn't bubbling it in dark enough. And the smell of those freshly printed test papers—like, the mimeograph ones? They always smelled so strongly of that weird ink. Some kids used to sniff the paper right when the teacher handed it out. 

Kids are so weird. My nephew is in middle school now, and he's obsessed with these little finger skateboards. Tech Decks, I think they're called? He'll just sit there at the dinner table trying to do kickflips over the salt shaker. My sister gets so mad at him, but honestly, it's kind of impressive that he can get the tiny board to flip like that just using two fingers. I tried it once and just ended up flicking it straight into the mashed potatoes. Mashed potatoes are so hard to get out of things, especially if they dry. You have to soak the plates forever. I always tell the guys at work to rinse their dishes out in the breakroom sink, but they just leave them sitting there...

Anyway, what was the question? A comprehensive evaluation? No, I don't think I've ever had anything like that. Just the basic physicals for work.
Can you tell me more about what you experience when you're trying to focus on a task, and how that affects your daily life?

Well, it's like... I'll start doing something, like looking at a digital work order on my tablet, right? I'll pull it up thinking, okay, I've got this, I just need to read the tenant's notes. But then halfway through reading it, my mind just completely slips off. Like, I'll hear a truck backing up outside—beep, beep, beep—and suddenly I'm thinking about the garbage trucks and how they always tear up the grass near the dumpsters at the Oakwood complex. The drivers just cut the corner too sharp. I've had to throw down grass seed there like three times this spring, and it never takes because the soil is too compacted. You really need to aerate it first, maybe get one of those core aerators that pulls the little plugs of dirt out. Those things are heavy, though. You have to rent them from the hardware store and getting them up the ramp into the back of the pickup is a two-person job, at least. And my coworker, Dave, he's got this bad back from when he used to do roofing, so I end up doing most of the heavy lifting anyway...

Wait, sorry. I do that a lot. Um, what I meant was... I'll be reading the work order, get distracted by a noise or start thinking about the next job, and then I'll look back at the screen and realize I have absolutely no idea what I just looked at. I have to read the same paragraph over and over just to get it to stick. It makes everything take twice as long as it should.

patient.answer:
